Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at CuratePay is excited to move to a hands-on POC. Before we lock dates, two quick asks from our infra team:

- We'd like to schedule a 90-minute kickoff that includes a short prompt-review exercise and routing discussion.
- We want to run a short load test (10–15 minutes) during the POC window to validate rate-limits and token budgets for our high-throughput flow. Could Redwood advise on expected peak RPS and any quota bump process for hosted trials?

Proposed week: May 31–June 4. Ideal times are mornings PT.

Can you also share a sample agenda and any estimation of token burn for the prompt sets?

Best,
Samantha

Hi Samantha — great to hear. Thanks for the details.

Quick responses and proposed plan:

- Kickoff: we can do a 90-minute hands-on session that pairs a short prompt review (30 min), routing & KV cache discussion (20 min), and a 30–40 minute guided load test run.
- Token estimates: attaching a first-pass token_budget_estimate.xlsx. For the prompt set you shared in the demo, expect ~0.9–1.3 tokens/word; the workbook shows per-flow multipliers and a conservative 3x buffer for spikes.
- Quota bumps: for hosted POCs we can provision a temporary quota bump (subject to approval). I’ve flagged this to Evelyn (cc). Please confirm peak RPS targets and estimated concurrency so we can size the bump.

Proposed slots (PT):
- Tuesday, June 1 — 9:00–10:30
- Wednesday, June 2 — 10:00–11:30
- Thursday, June 3 — 9:30–11:00

Ben (SE) will lead the load-test run and monitor metrics; Monica (CS) will cover onboarding and acceptance criteria.

Attachments: poc_agenda_v2.pdf, token_budget_estimate.xlsx

Next steps: Can you confirm which slot works and share the final prompt set for the 30-min prompt walkthrough?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai

Cc: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC next steps — kickoff and capacity questions

Thanks Tim — we can absolutely run a synthetic multi-client load test from Redwood. A few operational notes:

- We typically run load tests as a coordinated two-party exercise: Redwood generates traffic to validate routing, autoscaling, and rate-limits while the customer runs a parallel client to validate end-to-end behaviour. We can do Redwood-only if you prefer.
- For hosted trials we recommend a temporary quota bump that covers 3x your expected peak for a 30–60 minute window; we will monitor and revert automatically.
- Please confirm expected max concurrency (threads) and average request size (tokens per request). If you don’t have exact numbers, share a representative sample and we’ll map it to the token_budget_estimate.

Proposed alternate slots (PT) week of June 7:
- Tuesday, June 8 — 9:00–10:30
- Wednesday, June 9 — 9:30–11:00
- Friday, June 11 — 10:00–11:30

I’ve attached Redwood’s fallback policy doc (redwood_fallback_policy.docx) so you can see how we handle graceful degradation if the quota burn exceeds thresholds during tests.

Action items for CuratePay:
- Pick a slot from the options above
- Share the final prompt set (JSON/CSV) and target concurrency

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
